Synopsis:
The ECB delivered its second rate hike of 2026, driven by energy-driven inflation stemming from the Iran war. Oil surged past $105/barrel, pushing bond yields higher and equities lower. Analysts broadly expect at least one more hike before year-end, though debate whether tightening will extend into a prolonged cycle. Key risks include stagflation, second-round wage effects, and food inflation from supply chain disruptions. Core inflation remains relatively contained but is forecast above target through 2028, keeping the ECB in a hawkish posture while growth fragility limits room to maneuver aggressively.
